item.title: E-R Model of Infra Cluster
item.description:
The INFRA module is a management hub made of infrastructure nodes, rather than a traditional cluster. It provides core services for the deployment. Each node is an autonomous service unit that runs components such as Nginx, Grafana, and VictoriaMetrics. Together, these nodes provide observability and management for database clusters.

There are two core entities in Pigsty’s INFRA module:

  • Node: A server that runs infrastructure components. It can be a physical server, VM, container, or Pod.
  • Component: An infrastructure service on a node, such as Nginx, Grafana, or VictoriaMetrics.

INFRA nodes usually also serve as administration nodes, which form the Pigsty control plane.

item.title: Comparison
item.description:
Comparison with RDS

Pigsty is a local-first RDS alternative under Apache-2.0. You can deploy it on your physical machines, virtual machines, or cloud servers.

This comparison uses two benchmarks: Amazon AWS RDS for PostgreSQL and Alibaba Cloud RDS for PostgreSQL. AWS is the global market leader. Alibaba Cloud is the market leader in China.

Aliyun RDS and AWS RDS are closed-source cloud database services. You can only rent them on public clouds. The cloud-vendor information below is a February 2024 archive based on PostgreSQL 16. The Pigsty column in Feature Comparison follows the current release. The Key Extensions version table remains a historical snapshot.

item.title: Infrastructure
item.description:
Production HA PostgreSQL needs monitoring, alerts, logs, time synchronization, DNS, and software repositories. The INFRA module provides these services. It is optional but strongly recommended.

Overview

The following single-node deployment diagram shows INFRA components on the right:

Component Type Description
Nginx Web Server Unified entry for WebUI, local repo, reverse proxy for internal services
Repo Software Repo APT/DNF repository with all RPM/DEB packages needed for deployment
Grafana Visualization Displays metrics, logs, and traces; hosts dashboards, reports, and custom data apps
VictoriaMetrics Time Series DB Scrapes all metrics, Prometheus API compatible, provides VMUI query interface
VictoriaLogs Log Platform Centralized log storage; all nodes run Vector by default, pushing logs here
VictoriaTraces Tracing Collects slow SQL, service traces, and other tracing data
VMAlert Eval Rule/Alert Evaluates alerting rules, pushes events to Alertmanager
AlertManager Alert Manager Aggregates alerts, dispatches notifications via email, Webhook, etc.
BlackboxExporter Blackbox Probe Probes reachability of IPs/VIPs/URLs
DNSMASQ DNS Service Provides DNS resolution for domains used within Pigsty [Optional]
Chronyd Time Sync Provides NTP time synchronization to ensure consistent time across nodes [Optional]
CA Certificate Issues encryption certificates within the environment
Ansible Orchestration Batch, declarative, agentless tool for managing large numbers of servers

item.title: Monitoring System
item.description:
The built-in monitoring system provides metrics, logs, and alerting. Logs and alerts also support audit and traceability. It can monitor Pigsty-managed clusters, existing PostgreSQL clusters, and external RDS services.

Monitoring Targets

Pigsty monitoring covers these core targets:

  • PostgreSQL clusters and instances (SQL performance, connections, replication, transactions, checkpoints, WAL)
  • Infrastructure components (Grafana, VictoriaMetrics, Alertmanager, Nginx, etc.)
  • Host nodes (CPU, memory, disk, network, kernel)
  • Other service modules (ETCD, MINIO/Silo, REDIS/Valkey, KAFKA, MYSQL, JUICE, VIBE, etc.)

item.title: Encrypted Communication
item.description:
TLS can provide transport encryption, server authentication, and client authentication. Configure each protection separately. Enabling server TLS does not make clients verify the server or make the server require client certificates.

Most TLS operational work involves certificate issuance, distribution, trust, and rotation. Without central management, services often skip verification or keep plaintext connections.

Pigsty manages PKI declaratively. Deployment creates a local self-signed CA, issues component certificates, and distributes trust. TLS is then ready for use.

item.title: Metrics
item.description:
INFRA monitors VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, VictoriaTraces, VMAlert, Alertmanager, Grafana, Nginx Exporter, and Blackbox Exporter. Targets come from roles/infra/templates/prometheus/infra.yml.j2; scrape jobs are defined in roles/infra/templates/victoria/prometheus.yml.

Component versions and enabled services affect the raw metric set. This page lists scrape targets, rules, and common metrics for the Victoria stack. See Monitoring System for site-wide counts.

Metric Definitions and Counts

  • Raw metrics: Produced by components or exporters. Read TYPE and HELP at /metrics for their types and meanings.
  • Recorded metrics: Computed from expressions by vmalert and queried in VictoriaMetrics. They have no independent TYPE metadata and cannot all be classified as Counter or Gauge.
  • Scrape status: up and scrape_* are generated by the collection system. up=1 indicates a successful scrape; database and application availability still require functional checks.

Histogram / Summary _bucket, _sum, and _count are different samples of the same metric family. Historical table rows, recording rules, and live time series count different objects and cannot be added together.

item.title: Grafana High Availability: Using PostgreSQL Backend
item.description:
You can use PostgreSQL as Grafana’s backend database.

This tutorial explains the Pigsty deployment system through these tasks:

  • How to create a new database cluster
  • How to create new business users in an existing cluster
  • How to create new business databases in an existing cluster
  • How to access databases created by Pigsty
  • How to manage Grafana dashboards
  • How to manage PostgreSQL datasources in Grafana
  • How to upgrade Grafana database in one step

TL;DR 

vi pigsty.yml # Uncomment DB/User definitions: dbuser_grafana grafana
bin/pgsql-user pg-meta dbuser_grafana
bin/pgsql-db pg-meta grafana

psql postgres://dbuser_grafana:DBUser.Grafana@meta:5436/grafana -c \
 'CREATE TABLE t(); DROP TABLE t;' # Verify connection string works

vi /etc/grafana/grafana.ini # Modify [database] type url
systemctl restart grafana-server

Create Database Cluster

You can define a grafana database on pg-meta. You can also create a dedicated pg-grafana cluster on new nodes.
